data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's entire case rests on a 'Checklist Paradox' keyed to checklist size/cognitive load: as checklists grow, non-experts blind-tick and compliance only tracks the answer in simple cases, failing in complex ones. But that causal story is not invariant to checklist design. A short, high-usability checklist (explicitly named in its own countercondition) can produce reliable tracking on complex cases without inducing load-driven blind ticking; or, conversely, a long checklist can fail on simple cases if a step is misread. So the claimed mapping 'complex -> compliance failure' does not follow from the problem's inputs and is not a genuine basis for arguing against the panel. The distinguishing evidence it offers (fail in atypical cases) is conditional on an unsupported load mechanism rather than on the reliability-vs-compliance distinction the problem asks about.
